root_cause.text: The inet fragment reassembly subsystem’s `fqdir_pre_exit()` only marked fragment queues as dead without flushing queued SKBs, leaving fragment-buffered packets holding conntrack references until after `nf_conntrack` netns cleanup ran and causing `pernet_ops_rwsem` deadlock/spin in the netns exit path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `fqdir_pre_exit()` from a simple `WRITE_ONCE(fqdir->dead, true)` helper to a full walk of `fqdir->rhashtable` that calls `inet_frag_queue_flush()` on incomplete queues, and it adds the same flush in `ip_expire()`/`ip6frag_expire_frag_queue()` when `fqdir->dead` is set; the commit message explicitly says pending fragment SKBs were “holding conntrack references” and that they must be flushed “before conntrack cleanup runs.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The inet fragment reassembly subsystem’s `fqdir_pre_exit()` only marked fragment queues as dead without flushing queued SKBs, leaving fragment-buffered packets holding conntrack references until after `nf_conntrack` netns cleanup ran and causing `pernet_ops_rwsem` deadlock/spin in the netns exit path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move `fqdir_pre_exit()` from an inline header implementation to an બહાર-of-line function declaration.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the inline definition of `fqdir_pre_exit(struct fqdir *fqdir)` from the header and replaces it with a plain function prototype declaration. The deleted body previously set `fqdir->high_thresh` to 0 and `fqdir->dead` to true using `WRITE_ONCE()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `fqdir_pre_exit()` is no longer compiled as an inline header function; instead, callers will use a separately defined implementation. The functional behavior implied by the removed body is preserved only if that out-of-line implementation performs the same threshold shutdown and dead-state marking, but this change itself mainly alters linkage and code organization rather than the semantics of the operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the premature fqdir-dead short-circuit from IPv6 fragment queue expiration so the normal cleanup path still runs.
intent_record.what: The code removed an early RCU-protected check in `ip6frag_expire_frag_queue()` that read `fq->q.fqdir->dead` with `READ_ONCE()` and jumped to `out_rcu_unlock` if it was set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer exits immediately when the fragment directory is marked dead; instead, it proceeds to acquire `fq->q.lock` and continue the normal expiration path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a dead-fragment-directory check in IPv6 fragment expiry to safely flush and exit during teardown.
intent_record.what: In `ip6frag_expire_frag_queue()`, a new check was inserted after `inet_frag_kill(&fq->q, &refs);` that reads `fq->q.fqdir->dead` with `READ_ONCE()`. If the fragment directory is dead, the code now calls `inet_frag_queue_flush(&fq->q, 0);` and jumps to `out` before attempting `dev_get_by_index_rcu()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this avoids continuing the fragment-expiration path when the fragment directory is being torn down. It prevents subsequent device lookup and related processing on a dead frag directory, and flushes the queue in that teardown case to ensure cleanup happens safely.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a pre-exit cleanup path that blocks new fragment creation, marks the directory dead, and flushes incomplete fragment queues before teardown.
intent_record.what: A new function `fqdir_pre_exit(struct fqdir *fqdir)` was added and exported. It sets `fqdir->high_thresh` to 0 and `fqdir->dead` to true using `WRITE_ONCE()`, then walks the `fqdir->rhashtable` with `rhashtable_walk_*()`, locks each fragment queue, and calls `inet_frag_queue_flush(fq, 0)` on queues that are not marked `INET_FRAG_COMPLETE`. The existing `fqdir_exit()` function remains unchanged in this hunk.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes a fragment directory transition into a pre-exit state: no new fragments should be created, the directory is marked dead for concurrent readers, and any incomplete fragment queues still present are flushed before final teardown. This reduces the chance of races with ongoing fragment lookup/expiration and helps ensure cleanup happens before destruction.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure fragment queue flushes use a timeout drop reason when none is provided.
intent_record.what: A default assignment was added at the start of `inet_frag_queue_flush()`: `reason = reason ?: SKB_DROP_REASON_FRAG_REASM_TIMEOUT;` before calling `inet_frag_rbtree_purge()`.
intent_record.how: If the caller passes no drop reason, the function now substitutes `SKB_DROP_REASON_FRAG_REASM_TIMEOUT` so fragment queue purges are always reported with a concrete reason instead of an unspecified one.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the fqdir dead-state early exit from `ip_expire()` so fragment expiration continues to run correctly.
intent_record.what: In `ip_expire(struct timer_list *t)`, the code block that read `qp->q.fqdir->dead` with `READ_ONCE()` and immediately jumped to `out_rcu_unlock` if true was removed, along with its accompanying comment. The function now proceeds directly from `rcu_read_lock()` to `spin_lock(&qp->q.lock);`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the timer expiration path no longer short-circuits when the fragment directory is marked dead. This means `ip_expire()` will continue into the locked expiration handling even if `fqdir` is in the dead state, instead of skipping the rest of the function at that point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid timeout accounting and flush the queue when the fragment directory has already been marked dead during teardown.
intent_record.what: The timer expiration path in `ip_expire()` now checks `READ_ONCE(qp->q.fqdir->dead)` after calling `inet_frag_kill()`. If the fragment directory is marked dead, it calls `inet_frag_queue_flush(&qp->q, 0)` and jumps to `out`, skipping the `IPSTATS_MIB_REASMFAILS` and `IPSTATS_MIB_REASMTIMEOUT` counter increments.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the normal timeout failure accounting from running when the fragment queue's directory is already being torn down. Instead, it flushes the queue immediately in the dead-directory case, avoiding use of a fragment directory that is no longer valid and aligning the expiration path with teardown state.

Remove the fqdir dead-state early exit from `ip_expire()` so fragment expiration continues to run correctly.

consistency_review.core_intent: Handle IPv6 fragment queue teardown safely when the fragment directory is already dead, including flushing queues and avoiding invalid timeout processing.
consistency_review.reason: Hunks 2, 3, and 6 all focus on teardown-safe cleanup for a dead fragment directory, but Hunk 1 does the opposite by removing the short-circuit in expiry and forcing the normal cleanup path, which is not consistent with the shared teardown-dead handling.

Prevent IPv6 fragment teardown/expiry races by detecting a dead fragment directory and safely flushing or exiting without further timeout accounting.

relevance_review.reason: The change only moves `fqdir_pre_exit()` from an inline header to an out-of-line declaration/definition. It does not address the root cause of not flushing queued fragment SKBs or the resulting conntrack/netns exit deadlock.

The changes directly address fragment teardown by marking the fragment directory dead and flushing queued fragment SKBs before netns cleanup, which matches the root cause of leaving fragment-buffered packets (and conntrack refs) alive until after nf_conntrack cleanup, causing exit-path deadlock/spin.

The change only adds a default timeout drop reason for fragment queue flushes. It does not address the root cause of fqdir_pre_exit() failing to flush queued SKBs before netns cleanup or the resulting conntrack reference/deadlock issue.

The change directly targets fragment queue expiration cleanup by removing the fqdir-dead early exit, which matches the root cause of dead fragment queues not being flushed and cleanup stopping too early in netns exit.

candidates.rationale: This teardown entry point is where fragment-directory shutdown occurs; the vulnerability stems from fqdir_pre_exit() not flushing queued SKBs before netns cleanup, so the pre-fix exit path around this function is directly implicated.

This dead-directory check short-circuits fragment expiry during teardown. The root cause describes that queues were only marked dead without being flushed, so bypassing normal cleanup here leaves SKBs holding conntrack references.
This early exit on a dead fqdir prevents the normal expiration/cleanup path from running. That behavior matches the bug pattern of leaving queued fragment buffers unflushed during namespace teardown.
This jump is the mechanism that aborts fragment expiration once the directory is marked dead, which can strand queued SKBs until after conntrack cleanup and contribute to the teardown deadlock.
This premature bailout skips the cleanup work needed to flush fragment queues. In the vulnerable path, that means conntrack-referencing SKBs remain queued during netns exit.

vuln_statements.explanation: This dead-directory check short-circuits fragment queue expiration once fqdir is marked dead, preventing the normal cleanup path from flushing queued SKBs and leaving conntrack references alive during netns teardown.
This early exit on a dead fqdir bypasses fragment expiration cleanup, which matches the root cause where queued fragments were not flushed before nf_conntrack netns cleanup ran.
This jump is the control-flow bailout triggered by the dead fqdir check, and it skips the fragment cleanup work needed to release buffered SKBs before namespace exit.
This premature bailout exits the expiration path without flushing fragment queues, allowing SKBs with conntrack references to persist into the netns teardown sequence.
